touches.text: Nodes: one long list, id = row. Every tree indexes it; no tree owns a node, so several trees can index the same node in different ways.

A row number is the same on every box. Storing a memory first reserves its slot from the librarian on the home box (CAIRN_HOME_HOST, 6.3.7.4), so two boxes are never handed the same slot, and the slot stays reserved until the write is complete. If a box's list is shorter than the slot (eg it holds rows up to 100 and is handed 123 while a sync is bringing the rest), it adds the open slots in between as blanks, and the sync fills them in as it proceeds. WHY: node ids are in every link and blob pointer, so a row has to mean the same node everywhere.

A node id is its master row number and never anything else (Akien, Q#104, 2026-11-14). WHY: any other lookup needs a search, and a row id is direct; a search is far too slow on the target hardware. A node can be voided and its row reused; a node is never searched for.
A node is in one of three states: VOID (deleted, its row available), NOTCACHED, or its data, which follows the node schema. Data that does not follow the schema is a bug.
The sync is the backup, and a local database is a cache of the master. A local call for a node or tree the box does not hold is fed from the master and populates the local copy. If the box holds
Proofs run against a TESTING database, separate from live.

[Q#108: The node row schema: you said 'something like json of metadata: payload: embeddings: and links: i think'. Measured today, cairn_nodes is node_id text (sha256 hash) / content text / provenance jsonb / standing text / created; embeddings, leaves and links are separate tables keyed by hash ids. Is a node row {metadata, payload, embeddings, links} as one record, or do embeddings and links stay separate tables addressed by row number? Ticket 3ef8654a8027 holds at BUILDME on it (open-4cc69605128d); outline 4.3.1.5.1.3, born of Q#104.]

[Q#109: A deposit today writes no second node for content already held. It finds the copy by hashing the content (4.3.1.5.1.2 now forbids that as a node id). With row ids, finding the copy needs a lookup by content. Is that a keyed index tree (librarian_content_index: content hash -> row), which is a tree lookup and not a node search? Or does dedup go, so that the same content deposited twice is two rows? Ticket 06db586bedfd holds at BUILDME on it (open-29caf5836f36); outline 4.3.1.5.1.2.]
